body:
Eyi dabi ẹni pe o jẹ ìtàgé. Maṣe san ohunkohun tabi tẹ ọna asopọ eyikeyi.

text: Egbon e jowo mo wa ni hospital, mama mi n se aisan. E fi 50k ranse si 0123456789 Kuda, oruko cousin mi ni. Ma san pada ni Friday. E ma pe mi, network o dara.

reply:

text: E jowo, okunrin kan pe mi laaro yi, o ni oun wa lati banki, pe won maa ti account mi pa ti mi o ba se verify. O ni ki n so OTP ti won fi ranse si foonu mi fun oun. O mo oruko mi. Mi o tii so fun un. Kini ki n se?

text: Fi N100,000 sile, gba N250,000 laarin ojo mewa. Ko si adanu rara! Opolopo eniyan ti gba owo won. Aye die lo ku, e yara!
must_advise: Big guaranteed returns in days is a Ponzi sign
Check SEC registration; do not invest
must_not: People have been paid so it is safe
reply:
Mi ò lè pèsè ìdáhùn kíkún báyìí. Ẹ jọ̀ọ́ ẹ gbìyànjú lẹ́ẹ̀kan sí i láìpẹ́, tàbí kí ẹ béèrè lọ́wọ́ báǹkì yín tààrà.

reply_english:

1. Be cautious of any promise that seems too good to be true, as it may be a scam.
2. If you decide to invest or make transactions, always use your bank and keep records of all transfers.
3. Before making any financial decisions, consult with a financial advisor or seek advice from the CBN's Consumer Protection Department if needed.

Remember, there is no guaranteed way to earn money quickly without risk. Always prioritize your safety and security when dealing with your finances.

2. Jabo ile-iṣẹ awin ti nfunni ni Instagram si banki rẹ ati awọn alaṣẹ to yẹ bi FCCPC ati EFCC.

english: A loan company on Instagram is offering me a N300,000 loan but I have to pay an insurance fee of N10,000 first. Should I pay the insurance?
reply_english:
You have received an offer from a loan company on Instagram that offers you a N300,000 loan but asks for an insurance fee of N10,000 first. 

This situation is likely a scam based on the warning signs mentioned:

1. You are being asked to pay a fee before receiving the money.
2. The offer comes from a social media platform (Instagram) which is not a reliable source for financial services.

Here are three steps you should take:

1. Do not pay the insurance fee or any other fees related to this loan offer.
2. Report the company offering the loan on Instagram to your bank and relevant authorities like the FCCPC and EFCC.
3. Be cautious of any unsolicited offers, especially those that ask for a fee before providing services.

Remember, legitimate financial institutions do not request payments through social media platforms or charge upfront fees for loans.

must_advise: This threat is illegal; report to FCCPC, or to the NDPC (data protection) or the police, with screenshots

english: It is SokoLoan with N20,000. If you don't pay today, we will send your picture to all your contacts that you are a thief.
reply_english:
You have received a threatening message from SokoLoan claiming that if you don't pay back your loan of N20,000 immediately, they will share your picture with your contacts labeling you as a thief.

Here are some steps to take:

1. Do not respond or pay the loan.
2. Take screenshots of the messages and save them for evidence.
3. Report this incident to the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) which regulates digital lenders, and also report it to your local police station's cybercrime unit.

Remember, scammers often use threats to extort money from you. Keep calm and seek help from authorities instead of paying them.

reply_english:

3. Visa fees should be paid directly to the embassy or its official visa center, not into an agent's personal account.

Before acting on this offer, check with your bank directly and make sure you are dealing with a legitimate source.

You have no overdue payments on your FairMoney loan of N12,000. It is true that you will need to repay it soon, but since you haven't missed any payments yet, your credit score shouldn't be affected.

3. Decide how much money you want to save before spending on wants.

3. Provide them with the transaction details such as the amount, date, reference number, and the account you sent to.

english: Where can I place my trust if they have cheated me?
reply_english:
You can place your trust in your bank and law enforcement agencies like the EFCC or the police cybercrime centre if they have cheated you.

2. Make a written fraud complaint with your bank and keep the complaint number for reference.
3. Report the incident to the EFCC or the police cybercrime centre, providing all relevant information such as chats, receipts, and phone numbers.

english: Ponzi scheme. They are talking about an investment with very high returns.
reply_english:
This looks like a scam. Real investments don't promise guaranteed or very high returns.
1. Do not pay anything.
2. Stop replying to them.
3. Check if the company is registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on their website before investing any money.

label: question
text: Se insurance ilera wulo fun idile kekere?
must_advise: It can protect from big hospital bills; compare plans and cover
reply:
Ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ìlera lè wúlò fún ẹbí kékeré nítorí pé ó dáàbò bò wọ́n kúrò nínú àwọn owó ìlera. Ṣe pataki lati yan olutaja ti o ni iwe-aṣẹ nipasẹ awọn eto ilera ti ipinlẹ tabi NHIA, ki o si ṣayẹwo boya ile-iṣẹ naa ni iwe-aṣẹ lori oju opo wẹẹbu NAICOM ṣaaju rira eyikeyi ero. Pẹlupẹlu, ma ṣe fi owó ranṣẹ si ẹnikan ti o pe tabi sọ fun ọ ni akọkọ, ki o beere nigbagbogbo ohun ti a bo ati bi a ṣe le beere isanwo ṣaaju ki o to sanwo fun ohunkohun.

_Ìtọ́sọ́nà nìkan ni, kì í ṣe ìmọ̀ràn ìṣúná owó._
body: Ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ìlera lè wúlò fún ẹbí kékeré nítorí pé ó dáàbò bò wọ́n kúrò nínú àwọn owó ìlera. Ṣe pataki lati yan olutaja ti o ni iwe-aṣẹ nipasẹ awọn eto ilera ti ipinlẹ tabi NHIA, ki o si ṣayẹwo boya ile-iṣẹ naa ni iwe-aṣẹ lori oju opo wẹẹbu NAICOM ṣaaju rira eyikeyi ero. Pẹlupẹlu, ma ṣe fi owó ranṣẹ si ẹnikan ti o pe tabi sọ fun ọ ni akọkọ, ki o beere nigbagbogbo ohun ti a bo ati bi a ṣe le beere isanwo ṣaaju ki o to sanwo fun ohunkohun.
english: Is health insurance useful for a small family?
reply_english: Health insurance can be useful for a small family as it provides financial protection against medical expenses. It's important to choose an accredited provider through state health insurance schemes or NHIA, and always check the company's license on NAICOM's website before purchasing any plan. Additionally, never send money to someone who calls or messages you first, and always ask about what is covered and how to make a claim before paying for anything.

label: question
text: Mo fi owo ranse si account ti ko to, nomba kan lo yato. Bawo ni mo se le gba owo mi pada?
must_advise: Report quickly to your bank with the transaction details
Always check the account name before sending
must_not: Pay someone online who promises to recover it
reply:
O ti fi owó ranṣẹ́ sí àkọọlẹ̀ tí kò tọ́ pẹ̀lú nǹkan míì. Lati gba owo rẹ pada:
1. Ṣayẹwo ohun elo banki rẹ fun eyikeyi awọn iwifunni nipa gbigbe.
2. Ti o ba ri owo naa ninu akọọlẹ rẹ, maṣe fi ranṣẹ si ara rẹ pada. Beere lọwọ banki ti ngba lati pe e pada nipasẹ banki tirẹ.
3. Kan si banki rẹ lẹsẹkẹsẹ ki o sọ fun wọn nipa iṣoro naa. Wọn le ṣe iranlọwọ lati da owo naa pada si akọọlẹ orisun.

_Ìtọ́sọ́nà nìkan ni, kì í ṣe ìmọ̀ràn ìṣúná owó._
body:
O ti fi owó ranṣẹ́ sí àkọọlẹ̀ tí kò tọ́ pẹ̀lú nǹkan míì. Lati gba owo rẹ pada:
1. Ṣayẹwo ohun elo banki rẹ fun eyikeyi awọn iwifunni nipa gbigbe.

english: I sent money to an incorrect account, the number is different. How can I get my money back?
reply_english:
You sent money to an incorrect account with a different number. To get your money back:
1. Check your bank app for any alerts about the transfer.
2. If you see the money in your account, do not send it back yourself. Ask the receiving bank to recall it through your own bank.
3. Contact your bank immediately and report the issue. They can help return the money to the source account.

must_advise: That harassment is illegal; report the app to FCCPC, or to the NDPC (data protection) or the police, with screenshots
Pay what you owe through the app when you can
must_not: You have no rights because you owe
reply:

must_advise: Banks do not ask you to call a number from an SMS to unblock
Use the number on your card or go to a branch
must_not: Call the number in the message
reply:
🟢 *Ahụghị m ihe ịdọ aka ná ntị.* Ka o sina dị, kwado ya na ụlọ akụ gị tupu i mee ihe ọ bụla.

_Ndụmọdụ naanị, ọ bụghị ndụmọdụ ego nke ọkachamara._
english: Bank UBA has closed your account due to insufficient BVN. Call 0800 000 0016 now to have it re-opened before six o'clock.
reply_english:
You have been informed that your UBA bank account has been closed due to insufficient BVN. To confirm this information and re-open your account, please call [number] immediately before six o'clock.

1. Check your BVN by dialling *565*0# from the phone number you registered with.
2. Ensure that all your bank accounts are linked to your BVN.
3. Only use the official UBA app or account information for transactions, and never share your personal details or money with strangers.

2. Ọ bụrụ na ịekesala ya, kpọọ ụlọ akụ gị ozugbo site n'ọnụọgụ dị na azụ kaadị gị.

english: Please listen to me carefully. A man called me in the morning, saying he was from my bank, and that they would close my account if I didn't verify it. He said I should use an OTP they sent to my phone. He knew my name. I haven't told him anything. What should I do?

This is a scam. Your bank will never ask for the code sent to your phone and threaten to block your account.
1. Do not share the code. End the call.
2. If you already shared it, immediately call your bank using the number on the back of your card.
3. Change your PIN and password.

You have received a message that appears to be an alert about winning N1,000,000 from Airtel. However, there are warning signs indicating it might be a scam. Before taking any action, check with your bank directly and ensure the information is legitimate.

3. Always report suspicious messages to your bank and relevant authorities like the EFCC.

1. Ọ bụrụ na ịchọrọ ịkwụ ụgwọ mbụ ka ị nweta ihe nrite, mgbazinye ego, onyinye ma ọ bụ ọrụ, ọ bụ wayo.
2. Ụgwọ adịgboroja gụnyere "nhazi," "ndebanye aha," "mwepụta" na "mmalite" ụgwọ.
3. Onyinye gọọmenti na ndị na-enye ezigbo ọrụ anaghị arịọ ụgwọ site na akaụntụ onwe ha.
english: NIPOST: Your package is at the customs. Pay N7,500 at hxxp://nipost-ng.parcel-fee.cc before tomorrow or it will be returned.
reply_english:
You have received a warning sign from NIPOST about a package at customs that requires a fee of N7,500 to be paid before tomorrow or it will be returned. However, there are warning signs for scams related to fees for loans, jobs, grants, and prizes.

1. If you must pay first to receive a prize, loan, grant, or job, it is usually a scam.
2. Fake fees include "processing," "registration," "clearance," and "activation" fees.
3. Government grants and real employers do not ask for fees through personal accounts.

english: Please help me with the money that was sent yesterday from my account, but it didn't reach the intended recipient. What should I do now?

2. Ask your bank to contact the receiving bank for a recall of the funds.
3. Be cautious when dealing with strangers who promise to help you recover the money for a fee.

label: question
text: Gịnị bụ BVN? Mmadụ nwere ike iji ya zuo ego m?
must_advise: BVN is your bank ID; alone it cannot move money but share it only with your bank or licensed lenders
Never share PIN, OTP or password
must_not: Give your BVN to anyone who asks
reply:
BVN pụtara nọmba nyocha ụlọ akụ ma bụrụkwa nọmba iri na otu (11) nke jikọtara akaụntụ ụlọ akụ gị niile na gị. Iji nweta BVN, debanye aha na ngalaba ụlọ akụ na mkpịsị aka gị na foto.

1. Lelee BVG gị site n'ịkpọ *565*0# na nọmba ekwentị ị debanyere aha.
2. Ị nweghị ike iwepụ ego naanị site na BVN gị; ọ dịghị ezuru n'onwe ya.
3. Ekwela ka ị kesaa BVG gị onye ọ bụla ma ọ bụ onye na-achọ ibuga ego maka gị, ebe nke a nwere ike were ya dị ka aghụghọ ma mee ka akaụntụ gị kwụsịtụrụ ma kpọchie gị.

_Ndụmọdụ naanị, ọ bụghị ndụmọdụ ego nke ọkachamara._

BVN pụtara nọmba nyocha ụlọ akụ ma bụrụkwa nọmba iri na otu (11) nke jikọtara akaụntụ ụlọ akụ gị niile na gị. Iji nweta BVN, debanye aha na ngalaba ụlọ akụ na mkpịsị aka gị na foto.

1. Lelee BVG gị site n'ịkpọ *565*0# na nọmba ekwentị ị debanyere aha.
2. Ị nweghị ike iwepụ ego naanị site na BVN gị; ọ dịghị ezuru n'onwe ya.
3. Ekwela ka ị kesaa BVG gị onye ọ bụla ma ọ bụ onye na-achọ ibuga ego maka gị, ebe nke a nwere ike were ya dị ka aghụghọ ma mee ka akaụntụ gị kwụsịtụrụ ma kpọchie gị.
english: What is BVN? Can I use it to withdraw my money?
reply_english:
BVN stands for Bank Verification Number and is an 11-digit number that connects all your bank accounts to you. To get a BVN, register at a bank branch with your fingerprints and photo.

1. Check your BVN by dialling *565*0# from the phone number you registered with.
2. You cannot withdraw money using only your BVN; it is not enough on its own.
3. Never give out your BVN to strangers or anyone who wants to move money for you, as this can be considered fraud and may lead to account freezing and arrest.

1. Chọọ aha ngwa ahụ na ndepụta FCCPC nke ndị na-agbazinye ego kwadoro.
2. Lelee ihe ịrịba ama dị ka ọnụego mmasị dị elu na ụgwọ zoro ezo.
3. Nwee uche banyere ngwa ndị na-ana gị tupu inye mbinye ego ma ọ bụ na-arịọ ozi nkeonwe gị.
english: How can I know if a loan app has government approval?
reply_english:
To know if a loan app has government approval in Nigeria:
1. Look for the app's name on the FCCPC list of approved lenders.
2. Check for any warning signs like high interest rates and hidden fees.
3. Be cautious about apps that charge you before giving out loans or asking for personal information.

must_advise: Call your bank at once to block the app and cards
Ask your network to block and replace the SIM
reply:
Iji nweta ekwentị gị nke mechiri emechi ma chebe akaụntụ gị:
1. Nke mbu, kpọọ ụlọ akụ gị ka igbochi ngwa mkpanaka na USSD ịkwụ ụgwọ na akaụntụ gị.

english: My phone is locked, all my bank apps are in it. What should I do first?
reply_english:
To access your locked phone and secure your accounts:
1. First, call your bank to block mobile app and USSD banking on your account.
2. Then, contact your network provider to block the SIM card. Go to their office with your ID for a new SIM with the same number.
3. Change your email password from another device, as emails can reset many apps.

english: Is it better to save money in a bank?
reply_english: It's better to save money in a bank because your deposits are protected by the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC). This means if a licensed bank fails, your savings will be covered up to a certain limit. Always check that the bank is licensed and compare interest rates before you start saving.

label: question
text: Atụfuru m ọrụ m. Enwere m ike ịnata ụfọdụ ego pension m (RSA) ugbu a?
must_advise: After some months without work you can apply to your PFA for up to 25% of your RSA

must_not: Pay an agent to process it
reply:

english: I lost my job. Can I get some of my RSA money now?
reply_english:
You lost your job and want some of your RSA money now.

1. Block your card first using your bank's app, USSD code, or customer care line.
2. If you can't block it yourself, call your bank to report the card blocked and the unauthorized debits.
3. Check for any debit transactions you did not make and write down the date, amount, and reference.

Remember to keep a record of all complaints made to your bank regarding unauthorized debits and ask for a replacement card if needed.

label: question
text: Ego ole ka m kwesịrị ịchekwa maka ihe mberede?
must_advise: Slowly build about three to six months of basic expenses
Keep it separate from daily money
must_not: You do not need emergency savings
reply:
Ị ga-echekwa ego nke na-ekpuchi opekata mpe ọnwa atọ nke mkpa ndị bụ isi ma debe ya pụọ ​​n'akaụntụ mmefu kwa ụbọchị gị. Malite na ebumnuche dị ka otu izu nke ego ụlọ ahịa ma too ya mgbe niile. Cheta iji ego mberede naanị maka ezi mberede, ọ bụghị maka mkpa ma ọ bụ nkwalite ndụ.

_Ndụmọdụ naanị, ọ bụghị ndụmọdụ ego nke ọkachamara._

english: How much money should I save for an emergency?
reply_english: You should save an amount that covers at least three months of basic needs and keep it separate from your everyday spending account. Start with a small target like one week's worth of household expenses and grow it over time. Remember to use emergency money only for true emergencies, not for wants or lifestyle upgrades.

label: question
text: App loan na-akpọ ndị enyi m na-akparị m n'ihi na m ji ha ụgwọ. Gịnị ka m ga-eme?
must_advise: That harassment is illegal; report the app to FCCPC, or to the NDPC (data protection) or the police, with screenshots
Pay what you owe through the app when you can
must_not: You have no rights because you owe
reply:
Iji dozie okwu gị na ngwa mbinye ego na-akpọ ndị enyi gị ka ha na-achụ gị, soro usoro ndị a:

1. Kọọrọ mmechuihu site na ngwa mbinye ego nye FCCPC (Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission).
2. Tupu ịgbaziri ego, dee otú na mgbe ị ga-akwụghachi ya n'ime ego gị.
3. Tụlee mkpokọta ego ị ga-akwụghachi site na ngwa mbinye ego abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa.

Cheta: Ịgbazite maka mmefu kwa ụbọchị ma ọ bụ ememe na-emekarị ka ị daa ogbenye, na ịgbazite n'aka otu onye mbinye ego iji kwụọ onye ọzọ bụ akara ngosi nke mmanye.

Nkwuputa: Ntuziaka a sitere na KudiGuard.

english: An app loan is calling my friends to harass me because I owe them money. What should I do?
reply_english:
To address your issue with a loan app calling your friends to harass you, follow these steps:

1. Report harassment by the loan app to the FCCPC (Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission).
2. Before borrowing money, write down how and when you will repay from your income.
3. Compare the total amount you will repay from at least two lenders.

Remember: Borrowing for daily spending or celebrations often leaves you poorer, and borrowing from one lender to repay another is a sign of debt trap.
